q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the accounts of the Government of India, the revenue receipts (earnings) of the Railways from Commercial Lines are classified under Major Head 1001.
2. In the accounts of the Government of India, the revenue receipts (earnings) of the Railways from Strategic Lines are classified under Major Head 1002.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, railway revenue receipts are split by line type: Commercial Lines earnings fall under Major Head 1001 and Strategic Lines earnings under Major Head 1002, so both statements are correct.

q: While exhibiting the accounts of a Strategic Line for inclusion in the Government accounts, a clerk books its working (revenue) expenditure under Major Head 3002. The correct Major Head for the working expenditure of Strategic Lines is:
e: Working expenditure follows the same line-wise split as receipts: Major Head 3002 covers Commercial Lines and Major Head 3003 covers Strategic Lines, so Strategic Line working expenditure belongs under 3003.

q: A work of capital outlay is executed on a Strategic Line of the Railways. In the Government accounts, this capital outlay is classified under:
e: Capital outlay is classified under the 5000 series: Major Head 5002 is for Commercial Lines and Major Head 5003 is for Strategic Lines, so capital outlay on a Strategic Line falls under 5003.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Internal Debt of the Central Government is classified under Major Head 6001.
2. In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the External Debt of the Central Government is also classified under Major Head 6001.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Under the List of Major and Minor Heads, Internal Debt of the Central Government is Major Head 6001, while External Debt is a separate head, Major Head 6002, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A clerk, while preparing a statement of the Central Government's accounts, proposes to exhibit the interest payments of the Central Government under Major Head 2051. The correct Major Head for interest payments of the Central Government is:
e: Major Head 2049 is Interest Payments in the Government accounts. Major Head 2051 is Public Service Commission, so the clerk's proposal is wrong and 2049 is the correct head.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 8443 from Major Head 8009 in the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account?

options.A: Major Head 8443 covers the State Provident Funds, whereas Major Head 8009 covers Civil Deposits
options.B: Major Head 8443 covers Civil Deposits, whereas Major Head 8009 covers the State Provident Funds, including the State Railway Provident Fund
options.C: Both Major Heads cover suspense transactions pending clearance
options.D: Major Head 8443 covers Cash Remittances, whereas Major Head 8009 covers Deposits with Reserve Bank

e: Major Head 8443 is Civil Deposits in the Public Account, while Major Head 8009 is State Provident Funds, which includes the State Railway Provident Fund, so option B states the distinction correctly.

q: A zonal railway compiles a return of loans and advances to Government servants, including House Building Advances granted to its staff. In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, such loans to Government servants are classified under:
e: Loans and Advances by the Central Government to Government servants, including House Building Advance, are classified under Major Head 7610 in the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, transactions under the suspense heads are classified under Major Head 8658.
2. In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, cash remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same accounting authority are classified under Major Head 8782.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Suspense Accounts are classified under Major Head 8658 and Cash Remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same authority under Major Head 8782, so both statements are correct.

q: An existing broad-gauge line is converted to a wider gauge under a sanctioned work, but the expenditure is initially booked under Plan Head 15. The work should correctly be classified under:
e: In the railway Plan Head classification, Gauge Conversion is Plan Head 14. Plan Head 11 is New Lines and Plan Head 15 is Doubling, so a gauge conversion work belongs under 14.

q: A second line is laid alongside an existing single line to increase section capacity, and a clerk classifies the work under Plan Head 11 as a new line. The correct Plan Head for this doubling work is:
e: Doubling, that is laying a second line alongside an existing single line to add capacity, is Plan Head 15. Plan Head 11 covers only construction of a new line, so the clerk's classification is wrong.

q: In the Works Programme of a railway, a work of yard remodelling is proposed to be shown under Plan Head 15. Yard remodelling, being a traffic facility work, is correctly classified under:
e: Traffic Facility works, including yard remodelling, are classified under Plan Head 16 in the railway investment classification. Plan Head 15 is Doubling, so yard remodelling belongs under 16.

q: The cost of computerising the reservation and accounts offices of a zonal railway is booked by a clerk under Plan Head 16. Works of computerisation are correctly classified under:
e: Computerisation works are classified under Plan Head 17 in the Plan Head list. Plan Head 16 is Traffic Facilities, so computerising reservation and accounts offices belongs under 17, not 16.

q: Expenditure on a work relating to railway research, carried out through the research organisation of the Railways, is proposed to be classified under Plan Head 17. The correct Plan Head for works relating to railway research is:
e: Works relating to railway research are classified under Plan Head 18. Plan Head 17 is Computerisation, so research works through the railway research organisation belong under 18.

q: A road over-bridge is constructed in replacement of a level crossing as a road safety work, and the expenditure is booked under Plan Head 29. Road safety works relating to road over-bridges and road under-bridges are correctly classified under:
e: Road Safety Works are split between Plan Head 29 for level crossings and Plan Head 30 for road over-bridges and road under-bridges, so a road over-bridge replacing a level crossing falls under 30.

q: A major bridge work, including its approaches, is executed on a zonal railway and a clerk classifies it under Plan Head 33 along with signalling works. Bridge works, including tunnel works and approaches, are correctly classified under:
e: Bridge Work, including tunnel works and approaches, is Plan Head 32 in the Plan Head classification. Plan Head 33 covers signalling and telecommunication works, so bridges belong under 32.

q: An electrification project for a section of a zonal railway is sanctioned, but its cost is proposed to be booked under Plan Head 37. Electrification Projects are correctly classified under:
e: Electrification Projects are classified under Plan Head 36. Plan Head 37 is the separate head for Traction Distribution Works, so a section electrification project belongs under 36.

q: Works of traction distribution on an electrified section are executed by a zonal railway, and a clerk proposes to classify them under Plan Head 36 along with the electrification project. Traction Distribution Works are correctly classified under:
e: Traction Distribution Works are classified under Plan Head 37, distinct from Electrification Projects under Plan Head 36, so traction distribution on an electrified section belongs under 37.

q: A new workshop, together with a production unit, is set up by a zonal railway and the expenditure is booked under Plan Head 41. Workshops, including production units, are correctly classified under:
e: Workshops, including production units, are classified under Plan Head 42. Plan Head 41 is Machinery and Plant, so a new workshop with a production unit belongs under 42, not 41.

q: Residential quarters are constructed for railway staff at a station, and a clerk classifies the work under Plan Head 52. The construction of staff quarters is correctly classified under:
e: Staff Quarters are classified under Plan Head 51 in the Plan Head list. Plan Head 52 covers amenities for staff, so construction of residential quarters for staff belongs under 51.

q: A work for providing additional passenger amenities at a station is sanctioned, but the expenditure is proposed to be booked under Plan Head 51. Works of passenger amenities are correctly classified under:
e: Passenger Amenities works are classified under Plan Head 53. Plan Head 51 is Staff Quarters and Plan Head 52 is staff amenities, so additional passenger amenities at a station belong under 53.

q: A building is constructed for a railway training institute, and a clerk classifies the work under Plan Head 64 as an unspecified work. Works of Training and Human Resource Development are correctly classified under:
e: Training and Human Resource Development works are classified under Plan Head 65. Plan Head 64 is Other Specified Works, so a building for a railway training institute belongs under 65.

q: A work of a zonal railway is not covered by any specific Plan Head in the investment classification, and a clerk proposes to show it under Plan Head 65. Such works are correctly classified under 'Other Specified Works', which is:
e: Works not covered by any specific Plan Head are classified under Other Specified Works, which is Plan Head 64. Plan Head 65 is Training and Human Resource Development, so the clerk's proposal is wrong.

q: A metropolitan transport project is taken up for a metropolitan city, and its cost is proposed to be booked under Plan Head 64. Metropolitan Transport Projects are correctly classified under:
e: Metropolitan Transport Projects form a separate Plan Head 81 in the railway investment classification, distinct from Other Specified Works under Plan Head 64, so the project belongs under 81.

q: The Railways pay lease charges to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, and a clerk proposes to book the capital (principal) component of the charges under Plan Head 21 along with rolling stock. 'Leased Assets — payment of the capital component of lease charges' is correctly classified under:
e: Leased Assets, covering payment of the capital component of lease charges to IRFC, is Plan Head 22. Plan Head 21 is Rolling Stock, so the capital component of lease charges belongs under 22.

q: In the accounts of a zonal railway, the allocation of a work is written as 'DF-5200'. This allocation indicates:

options.A: A work of staff quarters (Plan Head 51) financed from Capital
options.B: A work of amenities for staff (Plan Head 52) financed from the Development Fund
options.C: A work of passenger amenities (Plan Head 53) financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: A work of track renewal (Plan Head 31) financed from the Development Fund

e: In the allocation string, the letters show the source of finance and the figures show the Plan Head: DF means Development Fund and 52 is Plan Head 52 for amenities for staff, so DF-5200 is a staff amenities work financed from the Development Fund.

q: In the accounts of a zonal railway, the allocation of a work is written as 'RRSK-3100'. This allocation indicates:

options.A: A work of bridge renewal (Plan Head 32) financed from the Railway Safety Fund
options.B: A work of staff quarters (Plan Head 51) financed from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.C: A work of road safety at a level crossing (Plan Head 29) financed from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.D: A work of track renewal (Plan Head 31) financed from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh

e: In the allocation string, RRSK means Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh and 31 is Plan Head 31 for Track Renewals, so RRSK-3100 is a track renewal work financed from RRSK.

q: A zonal railway proposes a labour welfare work for its staff and seeks to finance it from DF-I of the Development Fund, which is meant for passenger and other railway user amenities. Labour welfare works are correctly financed from the subdivision of the Development Fund known as:
e: The Development Fund is subdivided by purpose: DF-I is for passenger and other railway user amenities, while DF-II is for labour welfare works, so labour welfare must be financed from DF-II.

q: An operational improvement work on a zonal railway is found to be unremunerative, and the railway proposes to charge it to Capital in all cases. Unremunerative operational improvement works are correctly financed from:
e: Under the Development Fund subdivisions, DF-III is meant for unremunerative operational improvement works. Such works are therefore financed from DF-III and are not charged to Capital in all cases.

q: In the salary bills of a zonal railway, the pay of officers is booked by a clerk under Primary Unit 12, which stands for the pay of staff. In the Primary Unit (object) classification, the pay of officers is correctly accounted for under:
e: In the Primary Unit object classification, Primary Unit 11 is Pay of Officers and Primary Unit 12 is Pay of Staff, so officers' pay in salary bills must be booked under Primary Unit 11.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Primary Unit (object) classification of railway expenditure, Primary Unit 11 stands for the pay of officers.
2. In the Primary Unit (object) classification of railway expenditure, stores issued to revenue works are accounted for under Primary Unit 27.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Primary Unit 11 stands for Pay of Officers, and stores issued to revenue works are accounted for under Primary Unit 27 in the object classification, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Part A of the Traffic Book deals with the apportionment of Coaching earnings, which comprise passenger earnings and other coaching earnings, including parcels and luggage earnings.
2. Part B of the Traffic Book deals with the apportionment of Goods earnings among the railways over which the traffic has passed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Traffic Book apportions through earnings in two parts: Part A deals with Coaching earnings, including passenger, parcels and luggage, and Part B deals with Goods earnings, so both statements are correct.

q: A clerk in the Traffic Accounts Office proposes to apportion the advertisement rent collected by a zonal railway among all the zonal railways in proportion to distance. The correct position in regard to Sundry Other Earnings is that they:

options.A: Are apportioned among the zonal railways in proportion to the distance travelled
options.B: Are accounted for centrally by the Railway Board
options.C: Form part of the Public Account of India
options.D: Accrue wholly to the railway on which they arise and are not apportioned, being local and miscellaneous receipts which do not arise from the carriage of traffic over more than one railway

e: Sundry Other Earnings are local and miscellaneous receipts that do not arise from carriage of traffic over more than one railway. Under the Traffic Book rules they accrue wholly to the railway on which they arise and are not apportioned.

q: At the originating station of a through consignment, terminal services are rendered by Railway P, and a clerk proposes to divide the terminal charges among all the railways over which the consignment travels. The correct treatment of charges for terminal services is that they are:

options.A: Divided among the railways in proportion to the distance travelled over each
options.B: Retained by the railway which renders the terminal services and not apportioned among the railways
options.C: Credited to the Railway Board for central distribution
options.D: Held under Traffic Suspense till the close of the financial year

e: Terminal charges are for services rendered at the originating or destination station by one railway. They are retained by the railway rendering the terminal services and are not divided among the railways over which the traffic passes.

q: A recoverable advance relating to a capital work is made by a zonal railway, and a clerk proposes to hold it under the revenue suspense head 'Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue)'. Miscellaneous Advances relating to capital works are correctly carried in the capital (Plan Head) classification under:
e: Miscellaneous Advances relating to capital works are carried in the capital classification under Plan Head 73, alongside Stores Suspense under 71 and Manufacturing Suspense under 72, not under the revenue suspense head.

q: Midway through a financial year, the General Manager of a zonal railway sanctions a re-appropriation of funds from one Sub-Major Head to another Sub-Major Head under Major Head 3002. The correct position is that such a re-appropriation, the Sub-Major Head being the unit of appropriation for revenue expenditure, requires the sanction of:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal railway
options.C: The Principal Financial Adviser of the zonal railway

e: For revenue expenditure the Sub-Major Head is the unit of appropriation. Re-appropriation from one Sub-Major Head to another therefore crosses the unit of appropriation and requires the sanction of the Railway Board.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For revenue expenditure of the Railways, the unit of appropriation is the Sub-Major Head.
2. For capital (works) expenditure of the Railways, the unit of appropriation is the Plan Head.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The unit of appropriation is fixed separately for the two sections: the Sub-Major Head for revenue expenditure and the Plan Head for capital works expenditure, so both statements are correct.

q: One zonal railway has to intimate a transfer transaction, which involves no financial effect, to the respondent railway, and a clerk proposes to send a Transfer Certificate for the purpose. A transfer transaction involving no financial effect is correctly intimated through:
e: A Transfer Certificate carries a financial effect for acceptance by the respondent railway. A transfer with no financial effect is intimated only for information through a TWFA advice, so that is the correct instrument here.

q: Under E-Recon, certain transfer transactions raised by a zonal railway remain unmatched and unaccepted by the respondent railway at the close of a month, and a clerk proposes to write them off. The correct treatment of such transactions is that they:

options.A: Remain outstanding under the head 'Transfer Railways' and are pursued with the respondent railway till they are matched and accepted
options.B: Are written off automatically at the close of the month
options.C: Are converted into cash transactions with the Reserve Bank
options.D: Are transferred to the Railway Pension Fund

e: Under E-Recon, unmatched transfer transactions remain outstanding under Transfer Railways in the books of the originating railway. They are pursued with the respondent railway till matched and accepted, and are not written off at month-end.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Safety Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares.
2. The Railway Safety Fund also receives a share of the cess on petrol and diesel.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Railway Safety Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares and also receives a share of the cess on petrol and diesel, so both statements are correct.

q: During a day, a station collects receipts from its cloak room and left-luggage office, receipts from retiring rooms and charges for the carriage of postal mails. Taken together, these collections are classified in the railway accounts under:
e: Cloak room and left-luggage receipts, retiring room receipts and charges for carriage of postal mails are all connected with coaching traffic and are classified as Other Coaching Earnings, not as passenger or goods earnings.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Other Coaching Earnings' from 'Sundry Other Earnings' of the Railways?

options.A: Other Coaching Earnings arise from activities unconnected with coaching traffic, whereas Sundry Other Earnings arise from the carriage of parcels and luggage
options.B: Other Coaching Earnings comprise receipts connected with coaching traffic, such as parcels, luggage, postal mails and platform tickets, whereas Sundry Other Earnings comprise miscellaneous local receipts, such as advertisement charges and rent and licence fees for the use of railway land and buildings
options.C: Other Coaching Earnings are apportioned among the railways, whereas Sundry Other Earnings form part of Goods earnings
options.D: Both Other Coaching Earnings and Sundry Other Earnings consist only of receipts from catering units and book stalls

e: Other Coaching Earnings are receipts connected with coaching traffic, such as parcels, luggage, postal mails and platform tickets. Sundry Other Earnings are miscellaneous local receipts such as advertisement charges and rent of railway land and buildings.

q: A clerk prepares the allocation of an item of revenue expenditure by placing the Primary Unit immediately below the Sub-Major Head. In the classification of railway accounts, the head immediately below a Sub-Major Head is the:
e: The classification hierarchy below a Sub-Major Head is Minor Head, and only below the Minor Head come the detailed and Primary Unit levels. The head immediately below a Sub-Major Head is therefore the Minor Head.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The transactions of a railway are broadly divided into three categories, namely cash transactions, transfer transactions and remittance transactions.
2. Transfer transactions between railways involve an actual movement of cash from one railway to another.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Railway transactions are broadly cash, transfer and remittance transactions. Transfer transactions are only book adjustments between heads or railways and involve no actual movement of cash, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A transfer transaction arises between two divisions of the same zonal railway, and a clerk proposes to route it through the books of the Railway Board under the head 'Transfer Railways'. The correct position is that transfer transactions between two accounting units of the same zonal railway are adjusted:

options.A: Through the books of the Railway Board under 'Transfer Railways'
options.B: Through the Reserve Bank Suspense of the Railway Board
options.C: Through the Pay and Accounts Office of the Ministry of Railways
options.D: Within the books of that zonal railway itself

e: Transfer Railways in the Railway Board's books is used for transfers between different railways. Transfers between two accounting units of the same zonal railway are adjusted within that railway's own books.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Plan Head classification of railway expenditure, Stores Suspense is Plan Head 71.
2. In the Plan Head classification of railway expenditure, Manufacturing Suspense is Plan Head 73.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Stores Suspense is Plan Head 71 in the capital classification, but Manufacturing Suspense is Plan Head 72, not 73; Plan Head 73 is Miscellaneous Advances (Capital), so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Station earnings collected on a zonal railway are remitted through the bank and the Cash Office, and the amounts are finally adjusted in the accounts of the Railways through the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank of India situated at:
e: Station earnings remitted through the Cash Office and bank are finally adjusted in the Government accounts through the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank of India at Nagpur, which handles railway transactions.

q: In the books of a zonal railway, the head 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' normally shows a debit balance. This debit balance represents:

options.A: The amount standing at the credit of the Railways with the Reserve Bank of India, being an asset of the Railways
options.B: Cheques issued by the Railways but not yet encashed
options.C: Remittances despatched to the Reserve Bank but lost in transit
options.D: Amounts recoverable from other Government departments

e: Deposits with Reserve Bank shows what the Railways have placed with the RBI. Its normal debit balance represents the amount standing to the credit of the Railways with the RBI, which is an asset of the Railways.

q: A debit balance under 'Reserve Bank Suspense' in the books of a zonal railway indicates:

options.A: Cheques issued but not yet paid by the bank
options.B: Amounts remitted to, or adjusted by, the Reserve Bank which have not yet been cleared or responded to in the Reserve Bank's accounts
options.C: Earnings collected at stations but not yet remitted
options.D: Deposits of contractors held by the Railways

e: A debit balance under Reserve Bank Suspense represents amounts remitted to, or adjusted by, the Reserve Bank that have not yet been cleared or responded to in the Reserve Bank's accounts, pending its advice.

q: In the books of a zonal railway, a credit balance under the head 'Cheques and Bills' represents:

options.A: Bills receivable from outsiders pending collection
options.B: Cash in transit between stations and the Cash Office
options.C: Amounts deposited with the Reserve Bank in excess of the balance due
options.D: Cheques issued by the Railways in payment of dues, which have not yet been encashed or paid by the bank

e: Cheques and Bills is credited when cheques are issued in payment of dues. Its credit balance therefore represents cheques issued by the Railways that have not yet been encashed or paid by the bank.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The correct classification of an item of railway expenditure must be followed even if no budget provision exists under the correct head.
2. An item may be booked under a wrong head merely because budget provision happens to be available under that head.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Correct classification is a basic rule of railway accounts: an item must be booked under its correct head even if no budget provision exists there, and availability of provision under a wrong head never justifies wrong booking, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: An error in the allocation of an item of expenditure is noticed in the middle of a financial year, and it is proposed to correct the classification with retrospective effect from the beginning of that year. The correct position is that a change in the allocation or classification of expenditure can be given effect only:

options.A: Retrospectively from the beginning of the current financial year
options.C: From the month following the month of detection, within the same year
options.D: At any time before the Appropriation Accounts are closed

e: A change in the allocation or classification of expenditure is not given retrospective effect within the year. Under the accounts rules it can be given effect only from the next financial year, so correction from the month of detection is not permissible.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The erstwhile revenue Demands for Grants 3 to 14 of the Railways are now exhibited as Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12 under Major Head 3002.
2. The erstwhile revenue Demands for Grants 3 to 14 of the Railways are now exhibited as Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12 under Major Head 5002.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: After the merger of the Railway Budget, the erstwhile revenue Demands for Grants 3 to 14 are exhibited as Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12 under Major Head 3002 for Commercial Lines working expenditure, not under capital head 5002, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A work of capital outlay is executed on a Commercial Line of the Railways, and a clerk exhibits it in the Government accounts under Major Head 3002. The correct Major Head for capital outlay on Commercial Lines is:
e: Capital outlay is shown in the 5000 series of Major Heads: Major Head 5002 covers capital outlay on Commercial Lines, while 3002 is revenue working expenditure, so the clerk's booking under 3002 is wrong.

q: In a workshop account, the cost of materials used for the periodical overhaul (POH) of rolling stock belonging to the home railway is initially debited by a clerk under Primary Unit 27. In the Primary Unit classification, such POH material cost is correctly accounted for under:
e: In the Primary Unit classification, material issued for periodical overhaul of rolling stock is accounted for under Primary Unit 35, which covers POH material, and not under Primary Unit 27 for stores issued to revenue works.

q: A sanctioned work provides for the complete renewal of track on a section, and a clerk classifies it under Plan Head 32 along with bridge renewals. Track Renewals are correctly classified under:
e: Track Renewals are classified under Plan Head 31 in the Plan Head list. Plan Head 32 is Bridge Work, so a complete track renewal work belongs under 31, not with bridge renewals under 32.

q: A zonal railway indents for the procurement of new coaches and wagons under its rolling stock programme, and a clerk proposes to book the outlay under Plan Head 22. Rolling Stock is correctly classified under:
e: Rolling Stock, covering locomotives, coaches and wagons procured under the rolling stock programme, is Plan Head 21. Plan Head 22 is Leased Assets, so new coaches and wagons belong under 21.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Depreciation Reserve Fund is credited by appropriation from revenue.
2. The Depreciation Reserve Fund is debited with the cost of renewals and replacements of assets.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is credited by appropriation from revenue to provide for renewal of assets, and it is debited with the cost of renewals and replacements actually carried out, so both statements are correct.

q: Capital outlay on a category of works which is exempt from dividend liability is incurred on a Commercial Line, and a clerk proposes to exhibit it under Sub-Major Head 01 of Major Head 5002 along with dividend-bearing capital. Capital which is free of dividend liability is correctly exhibited under:
e: Within Major Head 5002, Sub-Major Head 01 covers dividend-bearing capital and Sub-Major Head 02 covers capital free of dividend liability, so exempt capital outlay on a Commercial Line belongs under Sub-Major Head 02.

q: The pensionary charges of retired railway servants, including monthly pension payments, are met in the railway accounts by debit to:
e: Pensionary charges of retired railway servants are met from the Railway Pension Fund, which is credited by appropriation from revenue for this purpose, and not from the Capital, Safety or Development Funds.

q: A zonal railway wishes to finance a work which is chargeable to Capital, but for which adequate Gross Budgetary Support is not available, out of its own internal accruals accumulated for capital purposes. The fund created for financing such capital works from the internal resources of the Railways is the:
e: The Capital Fund was created to finance capital works from the Railways' own internal accruals when Gross Budgetary Support is inadequate. It is distinct from the DRF, which funds renewals, so option B is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK) from the earlier Special Railway Safety Fund?

options.A: RRSK is financed only by a surcharge on freight, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund was financed only by dividend
options.B: RRSK is a fund of the Ministry of Finance, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund was a fund of the zonal railways
options.C: RRSK was created in 2017-18 as a dedicated fund for safety-related works of renewal, replacement and upgradation, replacing the arrangement under the Special Railway Safety Fund set up in 2001-02
options.D: RRSK meets ordinary repair and maintenance expenditure, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund met pensionary charges

e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh was created in 2017-18 as a dedicated corpus for safety-related renewal, replacement and upgradation works, replacing the Special Railway Safety Fund set up in 2001-02, so option C is correct.

q: The Debt Service Fund of the Railways has been created primarily to:

options.A: Finance passenger amenity works at stations
options.B: Meet the cost of renewals chargeable to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Pay the salaries of the Railway Board establishment
options.D: Provide a cushion for meeting the debt and lease obligations of the Railways, including obligations arising from market borrowings raised through IRFC

e: The Debt Service Fund provides a cushion to meet the debt and lease obligations of the Railways, including servicing of market borrowings raised through IRFC, and is not meant for amenities, renewals or salaries.

q: At the Final Modification Estimates stage in January, a zonal railway is asked to base its review broadly on the actuals of the first:

options.A: Five months of the financial year
options.B: Eight months of the financial year
options.C: Ten months of the financial year
options.D: Three months of the financial year

e: Final Modification Estimates are framed in January. By then actuals for the first eight months of the year, April to November, are broadly available and form the basis of the review, so eight months is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Only a Single Account Current is now rendered by the Railways, the practice of rendering a separate Approximate Account Current having been dispensed with.
2. The Account Current is the monthly account rendered by a zonal railway, compiled from its books for the month.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only a Single Account Current is now rendered monthly by a zonal railway, the separate Approximate Account Current having been dispensed with. The Account Current is compiled from the railway's books for the month, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'remittance transaction' from a 'transfer transaction' in railway accounts?

options.A: A remittance transaction involves no movement of cash, whereas a transfer transaction always involves cash
options.B: Both are identical and are adjusted under the same head
options.C: A remittance transaction involves an actual movement of cash between accounting units, whereas a transfer transaction is a book adjustment between heads or accounting units without movement of cash
options.D: A remittance transaction arises only between two divisions of the same railway, whereas a transfer transaction arises only with foreign railways

e: A remittance transaction involves actual movement of cash between accounting units, while a transfer transaction is only a book adjustment between heads or units without movement of cash, so option C states the distinction correctly.

q: One zonal railway has rendered services to another zonal railway and has to intimate the transaction, which involves a financial effect, to the respondent railway for acceptance and adjustment. The intimation is correctly sent through:
e: Where services rendered to another railway involve a financial effect, the originating railway intimates it by a Transfer Certificate, which the respondent railway accepts and adjusts in its books, so option D is correct.

q: A passenger travels on a local train whose entire journey is confined to a single zonal railway, and a clerk proposes to apportion the fare among several railways. The correct position is that the earnings from such local traffic:

options.A: Accrue entirely to the railway on which the traffic is carried and are not apportioned
options.B: Are apportioned among all zonal railways in equal shares
options.C: Are credited to the Railway Board for distribution
options.D: Are held under Traffic Suspense till the end of the year

e: Earnings from local traffic confined wholly to one railway accrue entirely to that railway. Apportionment in the Traffic Book applies only to through traffic carried over more than one railway, so no division is made here.

q: Through goods traffic is carried over three zonal railways before delivery at destination. In the apportionment of the goods earnings from such traffic, the share of each railway is determined broadly in proportion to:

options.A: The number of stations situated on each railway
options.B: The distance the traffic is carried over each railway
options.D: The number of wagons owned by each railway

e: Goods earnings from through traffic are apportioned among the railways concerned broadly in proportion to the distance the traffic is carried over each railway, after providing for terminal charges, so option B is correct.

q: Although the Indian Railways work under one management, apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the zonal railways continues to be necessary chiefly because:

options.A: Each zonal railway pays a separate dividend to the Government
options.B: The Reserve Bank requires a separate account for every railway
options.C: Each zonal railway is a separate accounting and administrative unit whose financial results are worked out railway-wise
options.D: The earnings of each railway are taxed separately by the State Governments

e: Each zonal railway is a separate accounting and administrative unit and its financial results are worked out railway-wise. Apportionment of through earnings is therefore necessary despite the Railways working under one management.

q: In the railway accounts, the gross working expenses of a year comprise:

options.A: Only the ordinary working expenses of the year
options.B: Ordinary working expenses and dividend payable to General Revenues only
options.C: Ordinary working expenses and appropriation to Capital Fund only
options.D: Ordinary working expenses together with the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund

e: Gross working expenses comprise the ordinary working expenses plus the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund. Dividend and Capital Fund appropriation are charges on net revenue, not working expenses.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Journal from the Ledger in the books of a railway?

options.A: The Journal is the book of final entry, whereas the Ledger is the book of original entry
options.B: The Journal is the book of original entry in which transactions are recorded chronologically, whereas the Ledger is the book of final entry in which transactions are classified head-wise
options.C: The Journal contains only cash transactions, whereas the Ledger contains only transfer transactions
options.D: Both the Journal and the Ledger are rendered monthly to the Railway Board as Account Currents

e: The Journal is the book of original entry, recording transactions chronologically as they occur. The Ledger is the book of final entry, where transactions are posted and classified head-wise, so option B is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the classification of railway expenditure, the Primary Units are the object heads of expenditure, such as pay of officers and pay of staff.
2. A Primary Unit indicates the source from which an item of expenditure is financed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Primary Units are the object heads of expenditure, such as Pay of Officers and Pay of Staff, showing the object on which money is spent. The source of finance is shown by the fund in the allocation, not by the Primary Unit, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Pink Book' from the 'LAW Book' of a zonal railway?

options.A: The Pink Book lists staff quarters works only, whereas the LAW Book lists track renewal works only
options.B: The Pink Book is a list of approved stores, whereas the LAW Book is a list of approved suppliers
options.C: The Pink Book contains the works programme as approved and included in the Budget, whereas the LAW Book is the List of Approved Works sanctioned by the General Manager within his powers
options.D: The Pink Book is prepared by the zonal railway, whereas the LAW Book is prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General

e: The Pink Book contains the works programme as approved and included in the Budget. The LAW Book is the List of Approved Works sanctioned by the General Manager within his own powers, so option C distinguishes them correctly.

q: In the workshop books, the balance representing labour, material and on-cost locked up on jobs under the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is exhibited in the capital classification under:
e: The balance of labour, material and on-cost locked up on jobs under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is exhibited under Plan Head 72 in the capital classification. Plan Head 71 is Stores Suspense and 73 is Miscellaneous Advances.

q: The principal function of the Cash and Pay Office of a zonal railway is to:

options.A: Compile the Traffic Book for all the zonal railways
options.B: Arrange the disbursement of pay, allowances, pension and other dues to railway staff and pensioners
options.C: Conduct the stock verification of stores depots
options.D: Apportion coaching earnings among the zonal railways

e: The Cash and Pay Office is responsible for disbursement of pay, allowances, pension and other dues to railway staff and pensioners. Compilation of the Traffic Book and apportionment are functions of the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: An urgent and unforeseen item of expenditure arises on a zonal railway during the year, for which no grant exists, and it cannot await the next session of Parliament. Such expenditure can be met initially by an advance from:

options.C: The Contingency Fund of India, pending authorisation by Parliament and later recoupment to the Fund

e: Urgent unforeseen expenditure for which no grant exists and which cannot await Parliament can be met initially by an advance from the Contingency Fund of India under Article 267, pending authorisation by Parliament and recoupment to the Fund.

q: Moneys received by the Railways towards the Provident Fund of staff and towards deposits of contractors are held in the Public Account of India. Payments out of the Public Account:

options.A: Do not require a vote of Parliament, as the moneys are held by the Government in trust and are not its own revenues
options.B: Require a fresh Demand for Grants every year
options.C: Can be made only after the Appropriation Act is passed for the Consolidated Fund
options.D: Are treated as charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund

e: Moneys in the Public Account, such as Provident Fund and contractors' deposits, are held by Government in trust and are not its revenues. Payments from the Public Account therefore do not require a vote of Parliament.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. With effect from the financial year 2017-18, the Railway Budget stands merged with the General Budget and is no longer presented separately to Parliament.
2. Consequent on the merger of the Railway Budget, the Railways were exempted from payment of dividend to General Revenues.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget from 2017-18 and is no longer presented separately. Consequent on the merger, the Railways were also exempted from payment of dividend to General Revenues, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Gross Budgetary Support from Extra Budgetary Resources in the financing of the Railway Plan?

options.A: Gross Budgetary Support consists of market borrowings, whereas Extra Budgetary Resources consist of budgetary grants
options.B: Gross Budgetary Support is raised by the zonal railways, whereas Extra Budgetary Resources are raised only by the States
options.C: Both consist entirely of the internal resources of the Railways
options.D: Gross Budgetary Support is the budgetary support provided by the Government for the Plan, whereas Extra Budgetary Resources are raised outside the Budget, such as market borrowings through IRFC and institutional finance

e: Gross Budgetary Support is the budgetary support provided by Government for the Railway Plan. Extra Budgetary Resources are raised outside the Budget, such as market borrowings through IRFC and institutional finance, so option D is correct.

q: Under the focal point system adopted for the remittance of station earnings, the earnings collected at stations are remitted to:

options.A: The Reserve Bank of India at Nagpur directly by every station
options.B: The focal point branch of the accredited bank nominated for the purpose
options.C: The Railway Board's Cash Office at Delhi
options.D: The Pay and Accounts Office of the Ministry of Railways

e: Under the focal point system, station earnings are remitted to the focal point branch of the accredited bank nominated for the area, from where they are passed on for adjustment against Deposits with Reserve Bank.

q: The Debt Head Report rendered by a zonal railway shows:

options.A: Only the balances under the Provident Fund head
options.B: Only the cash balance held in the Cash Office
options.C: The outstanding balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads of account
options.D: The variations between the Budget Estimates and the Revised Estimates

e: The Debt Head Report shows the outstanding balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads of account, so that old outstandings under each head can be reviewed and pursued for clearance.

q: 'Link heads' in the accounts serve the purpose of:

options.A: Linking the commercial accounts of the Railways with the Government accounts, so that the railway transactions are correctly incorporated in the accounts of the Government of India
options.B: Linking the accounts of one workshop with those of another workshop
options.C: Linking the salary bills of officers with those of staff
options.D: Linking the Traffic Book with the station balance sheets

e: Link heads connect the commercial accounts of the Railways with the Government accounts. Through them railway transactions are correctly incorporated in the accounts of the Government of India, so option A is correct.

q: Transactions arising between a zonal railway and the Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, pending clearance, are held under the head:
e: Transactions between a zonal railway and the Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries and Departments, pending clearance, are held under PAO Suspense. Cheques and Bills and Traffic Suspense cover different classes of transactions.

q: A debit balance under the head 'Demands Recoverable' in the books of a zonal railway represents:

options.A: Amounts due to the Railways from outside parties and other departments, which are pending recovery
options.B: Cheques issued by the Railways but not yet encashed
options.C: Earnings collected at stations but not yet remitted to the bank
options.D: Deposits made by contractors with the Railways

e: Demands Recoverable is debited with amounts due to the Railways from outside parties and other departments. Its debit balance therefore represents dues pending recovery by the Railways.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue)' from 'Miscellaneous Advances (Capital)' in railway accounts?

options.A: The former covers advances to staff for house building, whereas the latter covers advances for the purchase of bicycles
options.B: Both are exhibited under Plan Head 73 of the capital classification
options.C: Advances relating to revenue are held under the revenue suspense head 'Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue)', whereas advances relating to capital works are carried in the capital classification under Plan Head 73
options.D: The former is a remittance head, whereas the latter is a debt head of the Public Account

e: Advances relating to revenue are held under the revenue suspense head Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue). Advances relating to capital works are carried in the capital classification under Plan Head 73 as Miscellaneous Advances (Capital), so option C is correct.

q: The Appropriation Accounts of the Railways for a financial year are prepared primarily to:

options.A: Fix the earnings targets of the zonal railways for the next year
options.B: Compare the actual expenditure of the year with the final grant for that year and explain the variations between them
options.C: Apportion the coaching earnings among the zonal railways
options.D: Determine the dividend payable to General Revenues

e: Appropriation Accounts are prepared after the close of the year to compare actual expenditure with the final grant for that year and to explain the variations between the two, grant head by grant head.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sanction of a work by the competent authority does not by itself authorise expenditure on it; funds must also be allotted for the work in the Budget.
2. Expenditure on a work can be incurred only to the extent of the funds allotted for it for the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Sanction of a work and allotment of funds are two separate requirements: sanction alone does not authorise expenditure, funds must be allotted in the Budget, and expenditure can be incurred only up to the allotment, so both statements are correct.

q: The gross earnings of the Railways for a year comprise:

options.A: Passenger earnings and goods earnings only
options.B: Passenger earnings, goods earnings and dividend from subsidiaries only
options.C: Goods earnings and sundry earnings only
options.D: Passenger earnings, other coaching earnings, goods earnings and sundry other earnings

e: Gross earnings of the Railways comprise all traffic and allied receipts: passenger earnings, other coaching earnings, goods earnings and sundry other earnings, taken together, so option D is complete and correct.

q: Midway through a financial year, the General Manager of a zonal railway sanctions a re-appropriation of capital funds from one Plan Head to another Plan Head. The correct position is that such a re-appropriation, the Plan Head being the unit of appropriation for capital expenditure, requires the sanction of:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal railway
options.C: The Principal Financial Adviser of the zonal railway

e: For capital expenditure the Plan Head is the unit of appropriation. Re-appropriation from one Plan Head to another therefore crosses the unit of appropriation and requires the sanction of the Railway Board, not the General Manager.

q: A clerk proposes to treat the annual appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund as an item of capital expenditure. The correct treatment is that the appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund:

options.A: Is met directly out of market borrowings raised through IRFC
options.B: Forms part of the working expenses of the Railways and is charged to revenue
options.C: Is held under the Public Account pending utilisation
options.D: Is adjusted through the Traffic Book at the close of the year

e: The annual appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is a charge on revenue and forms part of the working expenses of the Railways. It is not capital expenditure and is not met from borrowings or the Public Account.

q: Under the Centralised Integrated Payment System (CIPS) adopted on the Railways, the position in regard to payments to vendors, contractors and staff is that:

options.A: Every station makes its own payments in cash to vendors and staff
options.B: Payments are processed through a centralised integrated system instead of being scattered across numerous local payment points
options.C: Payments can be made only after the close of the financial year
options.D: Payments are made directly by the Reserve Bank of India at Nagpur

e: Under the Centralised Integrated Payment System, payments to vendors, contractors and staff are processed through a centralised integrated system instead of being scattered across numerous local payment points, so option B is correct.

q: Under the Door Step Banking arrangement adopted for railway earnings, the correct position is that:

options.A: Station staff carry the day's cash earnings personally to the Reserve Bank at Nagpur
options.B: Earnings are deposited only once a month at the district treasury
options.C: The accredited bank arranges collection of the earnings from the railway premises themselves, so that cash does not have to be physically carried by railway staff to the bank
options.D: Earnings are retained at stations till they are adjusted in the Traffic Book

e: Under Door Step Banking, the accredited bank arranges collection of railway earnings from the railway premises themselves. Railway staff therefore do not have to carry cash personally to the bank, so option C is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cash-in-Transit in railway accounts covers the earnings collected at stations which are in the process of being remitted through the Cash Office and the bank to the Reserve Bank.
2. Keeping Cash-in-Transit low ensures that the earnings collected are credited promptly to the Railways' account with the Reserve Bank.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Cash-in-Transit covers earnings collected at stations that are in the process of remittance through the Cash Office and bank to the Reserve Bank. Keeping it low ensures prompt credit to the Railways' account with the RBI, so both statements are correct.

q: Transactions of a zonal railway with Public Sector Banks, which are pending clearance and adjustment, are held in the railway books under the suspense head:
e: Transactions of a zonal railway with Public Sector Banks that are pending clearance and adjustment are held under PSB Suspense, a suspense head meant specifically for bank transactions awaiting settlement.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'AG Suspense' from 'PAO Suspense' in railway accounts?

options.A: AG Suspense covers transactions with Public Sector Banks, whereas PAO Suspense covers transactions with the Reserve Bank
options.B: Both heads cover only the Provident Fund transactions of railway staff
options.C: AG Suspense is a revenue head, whereas PAO Suspense is a capital head
options.D: AG Suspense covers adjustments with State Governments and Accountants General pending clearance, whereas PAO Suspense covers transactions with the Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries and Departments pending clearance

e: AG Suspense covers adjustments with State Governments and Accountants General pending clearance, while PAO Suspense covers transactions with Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries and Departments pending clearance, so option D is correct.

q: At the beginning of a financial year, the annual allotment under a revenue head of a zonal railway is spread over the months of the year in keeping with the expected pattern of spending. This spreading of the allotment is known as fixing the:
e: Spreading the annual allotment under a revenue head over the months of the year, in keeping with the expected pattern of spending, is called fixing the budget proportions. It is the basis for monthly budgetary control.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'exchequer control' from 'budgetary control' over railway expenditure?

options.A: Exchequer control is exercised by Parliament, whereas budgetary control is exercised by the C&AG
options.B: Both expressions mean the same control exercised by the Accounts Office
options.C: Exchequer control watches the flow of cash and the balance with the Reserve Bank so that spending keeps pace with the availability of funds, whereas budgetary control watches expenditure against the allotment sanctioned under each head
options.D: Exchequer control applies only to capital works, whereas budgetary control applies only to stores purchases

e: Exchequer control watches the flow of cash and the balance with the Reserve Bank so spending keeps pace with availability of funds. Budgetary control watches expenditure against the allotment under each head, so option C is correct.

q: A zonal railway proposes to incur expenditure on a service which was not contemplated in the Budget of the year and for which no provision exists. Under Article 115 of the Constitution and the 'New Service / New Instrument of Service' rule (Finance Code), such expenditure:

options.A: Cannot be incurred without the prior approval of Parliament, obtained through a supplementary grant, save in the limited cases covered by the prescribed financial limits and procedures
options.B: Can be incurred freely by the General Manager by re-appropriation from any other head
options.C: Can be met from the Contingency Fund without any reference to Parliament at any stage
options.D: Is charged on the Consolidated Fund and needs no vote

e: Expenditure on a new service or new instrument of service not contemplated in the Budget cannot be incurred without prior approval of Parliament through a supplementary grant, save in the limited cases covered by prescribed limits and procedures under Article 115 and the Finance Code.

q: In an election year, the outgoing Government presents a complete budget for a transitional period instead of merely seeking a grant in advance for a few months pending the full Budget. The complete transitional budget so presented is an 'Interim Budget', which is correctly distinguished from a 'Vote on Account' in that:

options.A: A Vote on Account is taken after the Appropriation Act, whereas an Interim Budget is taken before it
options.B: Both are identical devices used only by the State Governments
options.C: A Vote on Account is a grant for the whole year, whereas an Interim Budget covers only one month
options.D: A Vote on Account is a grant in advance, voted by the Lok Sabha to meet expenditure for a part of the year pending the passing of the full Budget, whereas an Interim Budget is a complete budget presented for a transitional period, as in an election year, covering both receipts and expenditure

e: A Vote on Account is a grant in advance voted by the Lok Sabha for part of the year pending the full Budget. An Interim Budget is a complete budget for a transitional period, as in an election year, covering both receipts and expenditure, so option D is correct.

q: The salaries and allowances of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India and the judges of the Supreme Court are examples, in the Union Budget, of:

options.A: Voted expenditure, voted afresh by the Lok Sabha every year
options.B: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India, which is not submitted to the vote of Parliament though it may be discussed
options.C: Expenditure met out of the Public Account of India
options.D: Expenditure met by advances from the Contingency Fund of India

e: Salaries of the CAG and Supreme Court judges are charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India under the Constitution. Charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it may be discussed, so option B is correct.
